utterances.text: Yes. He was a salesperson from Cohodar Mahala. He was called Meho Pasalic or Pasovic. I'm not sure. He was also taken to the gate, and he never returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that it's B-43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How did -- these beatings that you described, how long did they usually last in the evenings? When did it stop?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Usually they happened after dinner. Night would fall around 9.00 or 9.30. It went on until 11.00 or 12.00, something like that, 11.00 or 12.00 at night. We can't really tell, but it lasted a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever hear shots in relation to such beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Shots were heard after these beatings almost every night when this happened. The shots could be heard in our room. These were individual shots, either from a pistol or an automatic rifle, but it was never a burst of gunfire, only individual gunshots. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: These detainees who did not return and who disappeared after such beatings, did you ever hear what happened to them? Did you have contact with their relatives? Do you know if they are still alive?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I didn't hear that any of these people were still alive. In that period -- I mean after that, a person was brought to my room, the father of that Veiz. Not Zulfo, the other Veiz. The salesperson, I mean. Munib. Munib. He was in my room, and he was asking about -- wondering where his son was. We did not want to tell him that he was taken to the gate and beaten. We wanted to make it easier for him. After I got out of the camp -- I don't know whether this is correct or not. I don't want to say whether it is true or not true, but some people said that this person, Munib Veiz, that his body showed up somewhere around Gorazde, that it had floated down the Drina River and that they found it on a bank by Gorazde. I'm not sure whether this is rumour or fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who told you that? Do you remember who told you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I can't remember who said that, but these were stories that were told by different people. I can't say who said that. These were stories that went around.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, rather early during your testimony, you mentioned already Juso Dzamilija, a salesman from Tabaci. Was he detained in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Yes, he was detained at the KP Dom. I did not see him in solitary confinement, but they told me that he was in solitary confinement. I found out only when he had hanged himself there. We were told that Juso Dzamalija had hanged himself in the solitary confinement cell. And I saw when, from my building where the solitary confinement cells were, a lady doctor went out in white uniform, followed by a nurse. They said that they were the ones who determined death in the case of Juso Dzamalija who had hanged himself in the solitary confinement cell. After that, the guards brought Juso Dzamalija out or, rather, they dragged his body in a white sheet. They were dragging him downstairs, and then they dragged his body all the way to the gate. We were told that he had hanged himself there. That's how we heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who told you that he hanged himself there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know who told me. Rumour had it amongst us, the inmates, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said that a doctor and a nurse were coming. How did you recognise or who told you that they were a doctor on a nurse?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Nobody said it. We assumed they were. The lady doctor was an older woman. They were dressed in doctors' white uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see them go into the building where the isolation cell was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: We didn't see them coming in. We just saw them coming out. After they came out of the building and climbed down the stairs, the guards came out dragging the body wrapped in a blanket and dragged it all the way to the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise Juso Dzamalija in this blanket.

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I cannot claim that I recognised it, but rumour had it that it was Juso Dzamalija.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said "rumour of it." Who told you? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Who told me, I don't remember, but there was another story circulating that Juso Dzamilija's son was a member of the special unit of the police in Sarajevo and that he came to Foca as part of a special unit and that that was probably the reason why the father was placed in solitary confinement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say -- did the guards actually speak about Juso Dzamilija's hanging himself or were the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Inmates were telling this story in their rooms, and how the story spread, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You were arrested together with six other villagers from Jelec. What happened to these other villagers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: All of the villagers who were arrested with me all survived the camp and were released.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let us now talk about some members of the prison staff. Who was the warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Milorad Krnojelac was the warden, nicknamed Mico.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did you learn this fact for the first time? Who told you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I learnt that as soon as I was brought to the camp. I was told in that room upstairs, Room 18, the people who were already there told me that the warden of the camp was Milorad Krnojelac. And he was around. We saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did staff members ever confirm the fact that he was the warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Everybody knew he was the warden. We were all there, and we all knew that there was no other warden. There was only him. He had a deputy by the name of Gagovic, and there was a commander of the guard or something, Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did you see Mr. Krnojelac for the first time in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know precisely. I saw Milorad most often in the yard when he was passing by on his way to the kitchen or to his office. He would go across the yard usually when we were not out for lunch or dinner. We usually saw him from our rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you saw him, what was he usually wearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: He had a military uniform on. Not a camouflage uniform but the olive-green/grey one. That uniform was worn not by regular soldiers but by noncommissioned officers or officers. He wore it with a yellow belt and a pistol in that belt.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This yellow belt, was it a particular soldier's belt?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Most probably a military belt since it was a military uniform. I don't know what kind of belt it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At what times did you see him? Did you ever see him late in the afternoon or the evenings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know, but I know he was passing by accompanied by some people, on his way to the carpentry shop. Sometimes it was evening, sometimes it was morning, but I don't remember ever seeing him at night. It was usually in the daytime, both in the morning and the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see him with heavy weapons? You mentioned before that he had a pistol, but did you ever see him with heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There was one day, I don't remember when, there were people playing football in the yard. Those were Serb inmates. Some wore uniforms, some didn't. I think it was in the afternoon. Later, they were all taken upstairs and locked up in their rooms. And those inmates who worked in the carpentry shop and elsewhere were returned to their rooms. We were all locked up. The door, the entrance doors, were all locked up, and everybody, including people who worked at the entrance and who worked in the carpentry shop - I don't know about the farm and other places, but all of us were locked up, and we were frightened. We could feel that something was going on. At that moment, guards appeared in the yard, all of them. They were carrying backpacks, military equipment, and at that moment the warden came out of the administrative building, carrying an automatic rifle, with a backpack on his back. They gathered in front of the kitchen. They assembled there, and went in the direction of the carpentry shop. We were afraid that they were going to kill us. However, they spread across the compound. I don't know where they were. But in any case, an hour or two later, they all came back and things returned to normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know what caused this particular situation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: We never knew what brought this about, but rumour had it it was some kind of drill or alert. That is what we heard later.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From whom did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: That's what we assumed, we the inmates, but there was no official information from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Krnojelac when detainees were taken away for exchanges or for beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I never saw him when people were taken away for beatings, but once when a lot of people were being taken for exchange, about 75 men, the warden, Krnojelac, was walking about the compound accompanied by Mitar Rasevic, and the guards, they were calling out people from their rooms and assembling them down in the courtyard. That's when I saw him. [as interpreted]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When was that? You said when 75 men were assembled -- detainees were assembled in the courtyard. When was that, what time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but in all probability, it was the 30th of August, the 1st of September, after the departure of those 55 people who had gone for an exchange. After their departure, it was the day after or two days later. All those people were assembled from their rooms, and according to our count and calculations, 75 men were gathered on that occasion, collected and taken to the gate. It was a fine, sunny day.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krnojelac present during the entire time when these detainees were gathered in the compound or only part of the time? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: He was present for some of the time while they were being collected from their rooms and assembled in the yard, I mean the prisoners for that big exchange involving 75 men. I cannot say he was in the yard all of the time, but I saw him on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you. When you described this situation when Mr. Krnojelac was with the heavy weapon, I forgot to ask you when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just have a small remark relating to the transcript. The witness said that Krnojelac happened to be in the courtyard. That's not what the transcript says. In fact, it's not in the transcript. Your Honour, it's page 97, lines 9, 10, and 11. He said, "Krnojelac happened to be in the yard," and after that, he said he wasn't there all of the time, only a part of the time. This second part is recorded well, but it doesn't mention that he "happened" to be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What I want to know is precisely where you say it fits in after the words "involving 75 men." Do you say he said Krnojelac "just happened to be in the yard"? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they were assembled in the yard, he "happened" to be there. He "happened" to be in the yard, in the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it would be best, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if you ask him precisely about that, perhaps by a leading question, so that we can get it cleared up. There is no way in which we can resolve that without having to go right through the tape. Would you ask him about it? It's disappearing off the screen, unfortunately. I've got it held on mine, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think the best is to clarify the whole situation, if it is by chance that he was in the courtyard or actually involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When these 75 people were taken, can you tell us how this whole procedure started? What happened on that day when these 75 detainees were taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: What happened on that day. Is that a question to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to this 75 people, how this procedure started.

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: It all began like this: The guards were moving around all the rooms, going from one room to another in the entire compound, calling people out and assembling them in the compound, where they lined them up. Those were ordinary guards moving about. At that time, there was also the warden moving around, walking about, and also Mitar Rasevic. During earlier exchanges, we didn't see the warden. We would see sometimes Mitar Rasevic, but even him we saw less often.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see the warden and Mitar Rasevic come together with the guards who collected the people into the compound or was he in the compound already for another reason? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was there in the yard for some other reason, but he was there. Down in the yard there was Rasevic, the warden, and other guards. The inmates were being assembled after being taken out from their rooms. They were being lined up, and Mitar Rasevic and the warden and the guards all took part in assembling the inmates. They were assembling this group of 75 men, and once they were assembled, they left.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How did Mr. Krnojelac take part in assembling these detainees? What did he actually do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know what he was doing, whether he was giving instructions to the guards or to other people, but in any case, he was around. He was there during the assembly of those people. What exactly his duties were or what he was doing, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The question is: What did you see him do? Did you see him talk to the guards who assembled the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know. He was just walking about. I can't say whether he talked to them or not, but they were just hanging about the courtyard, to put it in a vulgar way. Those guards were coming out of the rooms carrying lists. People were coming out, gathering. Down there in the courtyard, the people I have mentioned were present. What exactly he was doing, whether he had a specific task, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said they were just hanging about the courtyard. Was he close to the detainees or was he in another part of the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Of course he was moving among the prisoners who were being assembled from the buildings, from the prisoners' quarters, and he was walking close to them. I don't know whether he had exchanged a word or two with them, but they were all moving about the courtyard during the assembly of that group of 75 men. What their tasks were, I don't know, but he was present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And these 75 detainees, where exactly in the courtyard were they assembled? In which part of the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: They were being assembled and lined up directly in front of the gate through which they were going to be released from the building, in the narrow circle in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This may not be an ideal photo, but we will see.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7479.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are you able to point the assembling point out to us on this photo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Here, above the KP Dom. I cannot really find my way around this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can try two other photographs, and it's actually the photographs 7510 and 7511, which also show the yard.

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: This compound is a large space. That's in front of the door which leads out of the KP Dom. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you see this assembly --

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: It's in front of the door leading out of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you mean the metal door that you have already pointed out a couple of times?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: Yes, the metal door. Outside the metal door, somewhere before the metal door, and others were lined up on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me give you yet another photo, 7477. That's the bottom photo. If you look at this photo, can you show us where the detainees were lined up? Was it in front of this metal door?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: That is the metal door. This one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Look only at the bottom photo. Where were the detainees, these 75 men? Where were they lined up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: In front of this door and along this path. This is the metal door. You don't see the windows here that are next to it. Here, along this path.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at this path from the metal door to the left side of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where did you see Mr. Krnojelac? Where was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: They were moving along this path throughout the yard, outside building 1 and outside building 2. They were being assembled before the -- before leaving the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness has pointed out the same path again when he indicated where Mr. Krnojelac was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the matter. How long was he there? Do you recall? Just a couple of minutes or for longer?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I cannot know that. He was there. Whether he was there for two, three, or five minutes, I cannot say. I don't know. But he was there. He was there in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was he present when the detainees left through the metal door? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-69
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot claim one way or the other. I really don't know. While they were being collected and assembled and lined up, he was moving about the courtyard together with Mitar Rasevic and with the guards. He was there during the assembly of these 75 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is 4.00, and I would also now start a different chapter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, then, we will adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
